b.40b3da886f:
<h>Invitatorium</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Regem ventúrum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem ventúrum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>V</c>eníte, exsultémus Dómino, jubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem ejus in confessióne, et in psalmis jubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem ventúrum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu ejus sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus ejus <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus ejus, et oves páscuæ ejus.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem ventúrum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>H</c>ódie, si vocem ejus audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus jurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem ventúrum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Regem ventúrum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
b.869c7a0f72:
<h>Invitatory</h>
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord, the King who is to come * O come, let us adore Him.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord, the King who is to come * O come, let us adore Him.
<c>C</c>ome let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord, the King who is to come * O come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>or the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.
<r>Ant.</r> O come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>or the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. <n>(genuflect)</n> Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord, the King who is to come * O come, let us adore Him.
<c>T</c>oday if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
<r>Ant.</r> O come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>orty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord, the King who is to come * O come, let us adore Him.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> O come, let us adore Him.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord, the King who is to come * O come, let us adore Him.

<h>Lectio 1</h>
De Isaía Prophéta
<r>Isa 5:1-3</r>
<n>1</n> Cantábo dilécto meo cánticum patruélis mei víneæ suæ: Vínea facta est dilécto meo in cornu fílio ólei.
<n>2</n> Et sepívit eam, et lápides elégit ex illa, et plantávit eam eléctam, et ædificávit turrem in médio ejus, et tórcular exstrúxit in ea: et exspectávit ut fáceret uvas, et fecit labrúscas.
<n>3</n> Nunc ergo, habitatóres Jerúsalem, et viri Juda, judicáte inter me et víneam meam.
<h>H</h>æc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Ecce virgo concípiet, et páriet fílium, dicit Dóminus: et vocábitur nomen ejus
* Admirábilis, Deus, Fortis.
<r>℣.</r> Super sólium David, et super regnum ejus sedébit in ætérnum.
<r>℟.</r> Admirábilis, Deus, Fortis.

<h>Reading 1</h>
Lesson from the book of Isaias
<r>Isa 5:1-3</r>
<n>1</n> I will sing to my beloved the canticle of my cousin concerning his vineyard. My beloved had a vineyard on a hill in a fruitful place.
<n>2</n> And he fenced it in, and picked the stones out of it, and planted it with the choicest vines, and built a tower in the midst thereof, and set up a winepress therein: and he looked that it should bring forth grapes, and it brought forth wild grapes.
<n>3</n> And now, O ye inhabitants of Jerusalem, and ye men of Juda, judge between me and my vineyard.
<h>H</h>æc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Behold, the Virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, saith the Lord;and His name shall be called Wonderful, the Mighty God.
<r>℣.</r> He shall sit upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom for ever.
* And His name shall be called Wonderful, the Mighty God.

<h>Lectio 2</h>
<r>Isa 5:4-6</r>
<n>4</n> Quid est quod débui ultra fácere víneæ meæ, et non feci ei? An quod exspectávi, ut fáceret uvas, et fecit labrúscas?
<n>5</n> Et nunc osténdam vobis quid ego fáciam víneæ meæ: áuferam sepem ejus, et erit in direptiónem: díruam macériam ejus, et erit in conculcatiónem.
<n>6</n> Et ponam eam desértam: non putábitur, et non fodiétur. Et ascéndent vepres et spinæ; et núbibus mandábo ne pluant super eam imbrem.
<h>H</h>æc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Obsecro, Dómine, mitte quem missúrus es: vide afflictiónem pópuli tui: Sicut locútus es:
* Veni, et líbera nos.
<r>℣.</r> Qui regis Israël, inténde, qui dedúcis velut ovem Joseph, qui sedes super Chérubim.
<r>℟.</r> Veni, et líbera nos.

<h>Reading 2</h>
<r>Isa 5:4-6</r>
<n>4</n> What is there that I ought to do more to my vineyard, that I have not done to it? was it that I looked that it should bring forth grapes, and it hath brought forth wild grapes?
<n>5</n> And now I will shew you what I will do to my vineyard. I will take away the hedge thereof, and it shall be wasted: I will break down the wall thereof, and it shall be trodden down.
<n>6</n> And I will make it desolate: it shall not be pruned, and it shall not be digged: but briers and thorns shall come up: and I will command the clouds to rain no rain upon it.
<h>H</h>æc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> O my Lord, send I pray thee, Him Whom Thou wilt send; see the affliction of thy people. As Thou hast promised, come;And deliver us.
<r>℣.</r> Give ear, O Shepherd of Israel, Thou That leadest Joseph like a flock, Thou That sittest upon the Cherubim!
* And deliver us.

<r>Isa 5:7-12</r>
<n>7</n> Vínea enim Dómini exercítuum domus Israël est: et vir Juda germen ejus delectábile: et exspectávi ut fáceret judícium, et ecce iníquitas: et justítiam, et ecce clamor.
<n>8</n> Væ qui conjúngitis domum ad domum, et agrum agro copulátis usque ad términum loci: numquid habitábitis vos soli in médio terræ?
<h>H</h>æc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Ecce dies véniunt, dicit Dóminus, † et suscitábo David germen justum: † et regnábit rex, et sápiens erit, et fáciet judícium et justítiam in terra:
* Et hoc est nomen quod vocábunt eum: † Dóminus justus noster.
<r>℣.</r> In diébus illis salvábitur Juda, et Israël habitábit confidénter.
<r>℟.</r> Et hoc est nomen quod vocábunt eum: † Dóminus justus noster.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Dóminus justus noster.

<h>Reading 3</h>
<r>Isa 5:7-12</r>
<n>7</n> For the vineyard of the Lord of hosts is the house of Israel: and the man of Juda, his pleasant plant: and I looked that he should do judgment, and behold iniquity: and do justice, and behold a cry.
<n>8</n> Woe to you that join house to house and lay field to field, even to the end of the place: shall you alone dwell in the midst of the earth?
<h>H</h>æc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch; and a King shall reign in wisdom and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth:
* And this is His name whereby He shall be called: The Lord our Righteous one.
<r>℣.</r> In His days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell safely.
<r>℟.</r> And this is His name whereby He shall be called: The Lord our Righteous one.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> The Lord our Righteous one.
b.7252907722:
<h>Oratio</h>
<c>K</c>ýrie, eléison. Christe, eléison. Kýrie, eléison.
<n><k>Pater Noster</k> dicitur secreto usque ad <k>Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:</k></n>
<c>P</c>ater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
<r>℣.</r> Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
<r>℟.</r> Sed líbera nos a malo.

<r>℣.</r> Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
<r>℟.</r> Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>E</c>xcita, quǽsumus, Dómine, poténtiam tuam, et veni: ut ab imminéntibus peccatórum nostrórum perículis, te mereámur protegénte éripi, te liberánte salvári:
<h>Q</h>ui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre, in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.1bcf7c2300:
<h>Prayer</h>
<c>L</c>ord have mercy upon us, Christ have mercy upon us, Lord have mercy upon us.
<n><k>Our Father</k> is said silently until <k>And lead us not into temptation:</k>.</n>
<c>O</c>ur Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.
<r>℣.</r> And lead us not into temptation:
<r>℟.</r> But deliver us from evil.

<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>S</c>tir up, O Lord, we pray thee, thy strength, and come among us, that whereas through our sins and wickedness we do justly apprehend thy wrathful judgments hanging over us, thy bountiful grace and mercy may speedily help and deliver us;
<h>W</h>ho livest and reignest with God the Father in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>Q</c>uarto Nonas Decémbris Luna quarta. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>R</h>omæ pássio sanctæ Bibiánæ, Vírginis et Mártyris, quæ, sub Iuliáno Imperatóre sacrílego, ob Christum támdiu plumbátis cæsa est, donec rédderet spíritum.
<h>A</h>pud Forum Cornélii, in Æmília, natális sancti Petri, Epíscopi Ravennátis, Confessóris et Ecclésiæ Doctóris, cognoménto Chrysólogi, doctrína et sanctitáte célebris. Ipsíus tamen festum prídie Nonas hujus mensis recólitur.
<h>I</h>n Sanciáno, Sinárum ínsula, item natális sancti Francísci Xavérii, Sacerdótis e Societáte Jesu et Confessóris, Indiárum Apóstoli, géntium conversióne, donis et miráculis clari; qui plenus méritis et labóribus obdormívit in Dómino. Ipsum beátum virum Pius Décimus, Póntifex Máximus, cæléstem sodalitáti et óperi Propagándæ Fídei Protectórem elégit atque constítuit; Pius vero Papa Undécimus peculiárem ómnibus Missiónibus Patrónum dedit et confirmávit. Ejus autem festívitas, jussu Alexándri Papæ Séptimi, sequénti die celebrátur.
<h>R</h>omæ sanctórum Mártyrum Eusébii Presbýteri, Marcélli Diáconi, Hippólyti, Máximi, Adriæ, Paulínæ, Neónis, Maríæ, Martánæ et Auréliæ; qui omnes in persecutióne Valeriáni, sub Secundiáno Júdice, martýrium complevérunt.
<h>I</h>tem Romæ sancti Pontiáni Mártyris, cum áliis quátuor.
<h>I</h>n Africa natális sanctórum Mártyrum Sevéri, Secúri, Ianuárii et Victoríni; qui ibídem martýrio coronáti sunt.
<h>A</h>quiléiæ sancti Chromátii, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
<h>V</h>erónæ sancti Lupi, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
<h>E</h>déssæ, in Sýria, sancti Nonni Epíscopi, cujus précibus Pelágia pǽnitens ad Christum convérsa est.
<h>T</h>róade, in Phrýgia, sancti Silváni Epíscopi, miráculis clari.
<h>B</h>ríxiæ sancti Evásii Epíscopi.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.2c99f4fbaf:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>D</c>ecember 2nd 2027, the 4th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Rome, (about the year 363,) the holy Virgin and martyr Bibiana, who under, the profane Emperor Julian was for Christ's sake flogged to death with scourges loaded with lead.
<h>A</h>t Imola, (in the year 450,) holy Peter, Bishop of Ravenna, styled Chrysologus, (or him of the golden words,) famous for his teaching and holiness, whose feast we keep upon the 4th day of this present month.
<h>I</h>n the island of San-Chan, in the Canton River, in China, holy Francis Xavier, Priest of the Society of Jesus and Confessor, Apostle of the Indies, illustrious for the conversion of the Gentiles, for gifts and miracles, who fell asleep in the Lord, (in the year 1552,) full of good works and labours. Pope Pius X chose and appointed this blessed man the heavenly Protector of the Society and Work of the Propagation of the Faith, and Pope Pius XI gave and confirmed him as the special Patron of all Missions. His feast, however, is kept upon the morrow by order of Pope Alexander VII.
<h>A</h>t Rome, the holy martyrs the Priest Eusebius, the Deacon Marcellus, Hippolytus, Maximus, Adria, Paulina, Neo, Mary, Martana, and Aurelia, who suffered martyrdom under the judge Secundian, in the persecution under the Emperor Valerian, (in the year 256.)
<h>L</h>ikewise at Rome, (at the end of the 2nd century,) the holy martyr Pontian and four others.
<h>I</h>n Africa, the holy martyrs Severus, Securus, Januarius, and Victorinus, who were there crowned with martyrdom, (about the year of Christ 300.)
<h>A</h>t Aquileia, (about the year 409,) the holy Confessor Chromatius, Bishop (of that see.)
<h>A</h>t Verona, (in the sixth century,) the holy Confessor Lupus, Bishop (of that see.)
<h>A</h>t Edessa, (about the year 468,) holy Nonnus, Bishop (first of that see, and afterwards of Heliopolis in Syria,) through whose prayers Pelagia the penitent was converted to Christ.
<h>A</h>t Troas, in Phrygia, holy Bishop Silvanus, famous for miracles.
<h>A</h>t Brescia, holy Bishop Evasius.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
